To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the type of nonprotein energy in the diet affects energy utilisation for body growth, and that across fish species energy utilisation for weight gain is influenced by dietary nutrient composition.

the type of nonprotein energy (fat v. starch) affected energy utilisation for fish growth, that this effect was related to the digestibility of the respective macronutrient and to the composition of growth, that across fish species energy utilisation for protein accretion is higher than for lipid accretion, and that the relationships of energy utilisation for both protein and lipid accretion with dietary macronutrients were predominantly induced by the dietary fat and carbohydrate contents.
the type of nonprotein energy affects energy utilisation in fish and that energy utilisation for fish growth increases with increasing dietary fat and decreasing dietary carbohydrate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the type and level of dietary non-protein energy on energy utilisation for fish growth, and a literature comparison on energy utilisation across fish species.
the effects of the dietary macronutrients fat and starch on the digestible energy utilised for growth in fish.
the question whether dietary energy utilisation for maintenance and for growth can be predicted by the composition of dietary energy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the type and amount of NPE in the diet affects kgDE, which in turn is influenced by dietary nutrient composition.
the higher the proportion of fat and the lower the proportion of carbohydrate in the diet, the higher is energy utilisation for fish growth.
kgDE values are not constant across fish species, but are related to the composition of the diet, the composition of the fish and to the feeding level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
kgDE is higher in carnivorous fish species than in omnivorous or herbivorous species, and that kgDE increases with increasing dietary fat and decreasing dietary protein content.
the higher the fat content and the lower the carbohydrate content of a diet are, the more efficiently energy is utilised for growth.
the higher the fat and the lower the protein and carbohydrate contents of a fish diet, the higher is the energy efficiency of fish.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the type of NPE has a major effect on kgDE.
the type of NPE in the diet affects energy utilisation in fish.
the type of dietary NPE affects energy utilisation for fish growth and this needs to be considered when formulating diets for fish species.
